messages:
jess: Heads-up — thinking we should add an origin_stamp to rollout metadata to capture model provenance (upstream model id, artifact sha, quantization profile, build timestamp). Need to discuss max size, privacy, and merge semantics for rollbacks. Thoughts?

mike: +1 on provenance. Question: should we store full git SHA or canonical model-id + short-hash? Full SHAs can be big in telemetry and leak internal repo info.

sara: prefer model-id + semantic fields. e.g., { upstream: "llama2-70b", provider: "huggingface", model_hash: "sha256:abcd..." , q_profile: "int8-ggml" }. Keep it small and opt-in for private repo shas.

jess: proposal: origin_stamp string of form "provider:namespace/name@sha[:q=profile][+meta]" — compact, parseable. Example: `hf:meta/llama2-70b@e3f2a1:q=int8`. Also add a separate small metrics snapshot id that ties to evals.

mike: any concerns for customer PII? If customers deploy private builds we must avoid storing customer-unique identifiers unencrypted. Maybe we treat origin_stamp as controlled metadata and allow customers to opt-out / redaction.

sara: agree. For policy: redact anything matching regex of aws account ids, internal repo paths. Provide flag rollouts.allow_provenance=false at tenant level.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: new schema validated on staging, lint passed, no breaking changes for existing rollout readers.

jess: merge semantics: when a canary rollout is promoted to stable, we should append provenance chain rather than replace, up to N (3) entries. That helps debug which promotion path led to current variant.

mike: but chaining increases size. Keep chain entries compact: use short-sha (8 hex) + qtag + timestamp. And trim older than 90 days.

sara: one more: client-side resolver — if model pinned by client version and server sees different origin_stamp, client should surface a warning but continue unless strict_pin flag set.

jess: agree. Add strict_pin (boolean) in pin metadata. Default false. If true then on mismatch, reject request with HTTP 409 and reason includes origin_stamp_diff.

mike: schema snippet?

jess: include code block:

````
origin_stamp: "hf:meta/llama2-70b@e3f2a1:q=int8"
provenance_chain: ["hf:meta/llama2-70b@e3f2a1:q=int8+20250915", "internal:build/llama2@b1c2d3+20250916"]
pin: {
  strict_pin: false,
  client_pin_id: "client-v2.3.0"
}
````

sara: minor nit: no nested objects allowed in metadata transport proto? Our control plane uses flat kv map. So pin fields should be flattened: pin_strict=true; pin_client=client-v2.3.0.

jess: good catch. Make wire format flat. Use dot-separated keys for readability e.g., pin.strict=true in UI but stored as pin_strict.

mike: ops concern: telemetry and rollbacks — when rolling back, we should emit a rollback_event with previous provenance_chain entry and user causing rollback. That should be audit-only and not visible to clients.

sara: last: storage sizing. default allow origin_stamp up to 256 chars, chain up to 4 entries, each 64 chars max. That keeps DB column sizes reasonable.

jess: ok next steps: I'll open an RFC PR with the wire schema (flat map), opt-out flags, redaction rules, and migration plan for existing pinned models. @sara can you draft the tenant opt-out text? @mike can you write telemetry trim job?

mike: on it. ETA EOD.

sara: will draft by tomorrow morning.
